notes:
I can't give you any notes on Job 21 yet, because I wasn't able to read a single source page.

My first attempt to fetch the pages failed on a bug in my own code. I didn't capture any of the page text before it stopped, and the tool then stopped me from making any more requests. Your rules say to report only what the pages say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge, so writing verse notes now would mean making them up.

When I can make requests again, I plan to read these pages first:
- **Verse-by-verse sources:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/job-21/, plus the Ellicott, Pulpit and Gill commentaries on Job 21 at biblehub.com, and preceptaustin.org.
- **Modern scholarship:** the netbible.org notes on Job 21 (these may help with the Hebrew of vv. 16, 19, 24 and 33) and bibleodyssey.org.
- **Protestant traditions:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon (spurgeon.org), desiringgod.org, ligonier.org and thegospelcoalition.org, mainly on Job's challenge to the idea that the wicked are always punished in this life (vv. 7–34).
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** newadvent.org, which has the Church Fathers, including Gregory the Great's *Morals on Job*.
- **Prosperity teaching:** gotquestions.org or similar, but only if a page there actually links Job 21 to it.

If you'd like me to go ahead, just say so (for example, "continue"), and I'll write the notes verse by verse with a URL for every point.
